issues.problem: ZH title 看不出是升是落 carries the uncertainty ("cannot tell whether it is rising or setting"), while the EN title states only "Rising or Setting" without the inability to tell.
issues.suggestion: Consider "Can't Tell Rising from Setting: The Final Address Before Signing, September 17, 1787" or accept as a stylistic title rendering.

issues.problem: EN adds "— and asked what the alternative was" to Hamilton's remark, a piece of content (his asking what the alternative was) absent from the ZH text.
issues.suggestion: Add to ZH after the Hamilton sentence: 「并问除此之外还有什么别的选择」, or delete the clause from EN.

issues.problem: Stated motive for Gorham's motion differs: ZH says the change was proposed 以减少反对意见 (to reduce objections), while EN says only that the clause "had produced so much discussion", giving a different cause.
issues.suggestion: Change EN to "— a clause that had produced so much discussion and whose objections this might lessen —" or align ZH to "这一条引发了很多讨论".

issues.problem: EN adds content not in ZH: "Many members had thought the small proportion of representatives thin security for the rights and interests of the people", plus "deputy from Virginia" for Washington; ZH only has the president's own admission that the small ratio was exceptionable.
issues.suggestion: Add to ZH: 「许多人认为代表比例偏小不足以保障人民的权利和利益」 (and optionally 「弗吉尼亚代表」 after 华盛顿), or trim these from EN.

overall: The two editions match closely in facts, quotes and structure; the only real divergences are a few English-only additions and one shifted motive in the closing-day passage, plus a title that drops the ZH "can't tell" nuance.
